# 05c A styled edge carries its own arrowhead

## Outcome

`linkStyle 0 stroke:#f00` colors the whole arrow — line and head — as it does in Mermaid. And two
Siren diagrams on one page stop sharing each other's markers.

## Why this ticket exists

Ticket 05 pinned the truth rather than engineering around it: an edge's `stroke` recolors the line
and leaves the arrowhead the theme's color. There is one `<marker id="siren-arrow">` in `<defs>`
for the whole diagram, and SVG marker content inherits from the marker's own ancestors, not from
the path referencing it. Mermaid colors the whole arrow. That is a compatibility gap, and the repo
owner has asked for it closed.

**It has a prerequisite, measured:**

```
two flowcharts on one page  ->  ids = ["siren-arrow", "siren-arrow"]
```

`url(#siren-arrow)` resolves against the whole *document*, not the SVG, so the browser picks the
first match. Today that is invisible because every marker is identical. The moment markers carry
per-edge colors, **the second diagram's arrows would take the first diagram's colors** — this
ticket would ship a visible cross-diagram bug unless the ids are scoped first.

This is the same global-namespace problem ADR-0008 used to reject a generated `<style>` block
("two Siren diagrams on one page would have to coordinate their generated names"). It already
exists here; this ticket is what would activate it.

The class diagram has the identical exposure — `siren-class-triangle`, `siren-class-diamond-filled`
and the rest are also fixed ids. Fixing only the flowchart would be half a fix, and this board has
already been bitten once by leaving half a fix behind (ticket 11's `packages/board` tsconfig).

## Acceptance criteria

**Scoping first — it is the prerequisite, so land it first and prove it separately**

- [x] Marker ids are unique per rendered SVG, in **both** the flowchart and class-diagram
      renderers. Two diagrams rendered onto one page share no id at all — assert by collecting
      every `[id]` in the page and checking for duplicates, the way the probe that found this did.
- [x] Every `url(#...)` reference resolves within its own SVG. Assert that the second diagram's
      edges reference the second diagram's marker, not the first's.
- [x] The scheme is stated where it is generated, including why document-scoped ids are the hazard.

**Then the arrowhead**

- [x] An edge whose author style sets `stroke` gets an arrowhead of that color. Assert the marker's
      fill, not merely that a second marker exists.
- [x] An edge nothing styled still uses the theme's shared marker, and no per-edge marker is minted
      for it — a diagram with no `linkStyle` emits exactly the markers it emits today.
- [x] Decide and justify: one marker per *styled edge*, or one per *distinct stroke color*. Both are
      defensible; say which and why in your report. Consider what happens with 50 edges sharing one
      color.
- [x] A `linkStyle` that sets no `stroke` (say `stroke-width` alone) does not mint a marker — there
      is no color to carry.
- [x] The theme still governs an unstyled arrowhead. `--siren-edge-stroke` must keep working, and a
      consumer redeclaring it must still recolor every unstyled arrow.
- [x] Ticket 05's test pinning "an edge's stroke leaves the arrowhead the theme's color" asserted a
      truth this ticket reverses. Update it and call that out in your report as the intended change.

## Test seam

`render()` for both halves — id uniqueness is only observable with two diagrams in one document,
and marker fill is only observable in the rendered SVG.

## Write ownership

- `packages/core/src/renderer/renderToSVG.ts` + `.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/renderer/renderClassDiagramToSVG.ts` + `.test.ts` (scoping half only)
- `packages/core/src/theme/default.css` + `default.test.ts` (only if the scoping scheme needs it)
- `packages/core/src/index.test.ts`

## Shared resources

None — runs alone.

## Blocked by

- **05b** — it shares `index.test.ts`, and its tier changes what an edge's resolved stroke *is*,
  which is the input this ticket draws a marker from.

## Status

Done (2026-09-05), commit 1c1a4ba. 7 slices (4 red-green, 3 declared guards, one with a disclosed
double mutation check). 581 core tests / 29 board, tsc clean both.

Integrator verified independently: four diagrams on one page → 10 ids, zero duplicates; three edges
in two colors → three markers (theme + red + green).

Disclosed cost: markup is no longer byte-reproducible across renders, and three existing tests
normalize one token. The helper is `/__[0-9a-z]{8}(?![0-9a-z])/g` — checked, and as narrow as
claimed.

Left for 05d: the sequence renderer's marker ids are still fixed, so the no-duplicate-ids property
holds for flowchart and class diagrams but not repo-wide.

## Done when

Every criterion is checked, `pnpm -r test` is green, `tsc --noEmit` is clean in both packages, and
two diagrams on one page render independently.
